verses.zh: （上行之诗。）耶和华啊，求你记念大卫所受的一切苦难！
verses.en: A song of ascents.[NOTE:1] O Lord, for David’s sake rememberall his strenuous effort[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 132. The psalmist reminds God of David’s devotion and of his promises concerning David’s dynasty and Zion.

The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.
verses.commentary:
132:1 "Remember" This is an IMPERATIVE used as a prayer. Psalm 25:6-7 shows the way this was used.

- God, remember Your unchanging character of grace and mercy, Ps. 25:6

- God, forget our sin, Ps. 25:7

▣ "O Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "on David's behalf" Often the people of Israel and her leaders asked God to have mercy on them because of

- His promises to the Fathers (i.e., Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob)

- His promises to David (cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17; 2 Chronicles 6:16)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "All his affliction" This seems to allude to David's statements in 2 Sam. 16:12, but it may refer to David's
initial problems in bringing the ark into Jerusalem (cf. 2 Samuel 6; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT). The JPSOA translates it as "his extreme self-denial," which
would relate to its usage in Num. 30:13 and 1 Chr. 22:14.

The LXX revocalizes the MT (BDB 776 III, KB 853, Pual INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) to
"his meekness" (a NOUN, BDB 776, cf. Ps. 45:4).

verses.zh: 他怎样向耶和华起誓，向雅各的大能者许愿，
verses.en: and how he made a vow to the Lord,and swore an oath to the Powerful One of Jacob.
verses.commentary:
132:2-5 "he swore to the Lord" This oath is not recorded in the
historical books. Basically David

- made a vow about the tabernacle being brought to Jerusalem

- would not enter his own dwelling place (lit. "the tent of my house") until the tabernacle (i.e., YHWH's
tent of dwelling) was in Jerusalem

- would not sleep (hyperbolic) until the ark came

- Ps. 132:5 states his purpose (i.e., the ark of the covenant and the tabernacle in his capital, cf. Acts 7:46)

It is obvious that #2 and #3 are hyperbolic and used in a literary fashion to show intense intent!

132:2 "the Mighty One of Jacob" This title (BDB 7 CONSTRUCT BDB 784) for Israel's Deity is first
used in Gen. 49:24, where Jacob blesses his children, the future tribes of Israel. It is also used in Isa. 49:26 (promise of
universal redemption) and 60:16, where it is linked with other titles for YHWH.

- Savior (cf. Isa. 19:2; 43:3,11; 45:15,21; 63:8; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR)

- Redeemer (cf. Isa. 59:20; 63:16;
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)

The NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 232, has the interesting comment that the ADJECTIVE "mighty" has two forms.

- originally it referred to the strength of bulls or wild oxen

- to designate YHWH's power

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 说：我必不进我的帐幕，也不上我的床榻；
verses.en: He said,[NOTE:1] “I will not enter my own home,[NOTE:2] or get into my bed.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all his affliction.” This may refer to David’s strenuous and tireless efforts to make provision for the building of the temple (see 1 Chr 22:14). Some prefer to revocalize the text as עַנַוָתוֹ (ʿanavato, “his humility”).
The words “he said” are supplied in the translation to clarify that what follows is David’s vow.
Heb “the tent of my house.”

verses.zh: 我不容我的眼睛睡觉，也不容我的眼目打盹；
verses.en: I will not allow my eyes to sleepor my eyelids to slumber,

verses.zh: 直等我为耶和华寻得所在，为雅各的大能者寻得居所。
verses.en: until I find a place for the Lord,a fine dwelling place[NOTE:1] for the Powerful One of Jacob.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “go up upon the bed of my couch.”
The plural form of the noun may indicate degree or quality; David envisions a special dwelling place (see Pss 43:3; 46:4; 84:1).
verses.commentary:
132:5 This is not referring to David's desire to build a permanent temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:17; 1 Chr. 22:7) but to
bringing the ark, along with its portable tent (i.e., tabernacle of the exodus period) into his capital, Jerusalem (cf. 2 Samuel 6).

▣ "dwelling place" This is PLURAL in the MT and may be a grammatical way
to denote significance.

In other contexts this term in the PLURAL denotes all the buildings in the
temple enclosure (cf. Ps. 43:3; 46:4; 84:1).

verses.zh: 我们听说约柜在以法他，我们在基列・耶琳就寻见了。
verses.en: Look, we heard about it[NOTE:1] in Ephrathah;[NOTE:2] we found it in the territory of Jaar.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “the Mighty One of Jacob.”

Rather than having an antecedent, the third feminine singular pronominal suffix here (and in the next line) appears to refer to the ark of the covenant, mentioned in v. 8. (The Hebrew term אָרוֹן [ʾaron, “ark”] is sometimes construed as grammatically feminine. See 1 Sam 4:17; 2 Chr 8:11.)

Some understand Ephrathah as a reference to Kiriath Jearim because of the apparent allusion to this site in the next line (see the note on “Jaar”). The ark was kept in Kiriath Jearim after the Philistines released it (see 1 Sam 6:21-7:2). However, the switch in verbs from “heard about” to “found” suggests that Ephrathah not be equated with Jair. The group who is speaking heard about the ark while they were in Ephrath. They then went to retrieve it from Kiriath Jearim (“Jaar”). It is more likely that Ephrathah refers to a site near Bethel (Gen 35:16, 19; 48:7) or to Bethlehem (Ruth 4:11; Mic 5:2).
verses.commentary:
132:6 "Ephrathah" is an area in Judah (cf. Micah 5:2) which came to refer to the extended family of David (cf. Ruth 4:11).
However, Bethlehem was not the location of the ark. They just heard about the King's oath (cf. Ps. 132:2) to bring the ark to Jerusalem.

▣ "it" This is a FEMININE suffix, while "the ark" is MASCULINE, so it may
refer to David's oath (NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 736; AB, p. 244) mentioned in Ps. 132:2.

The NEB (p. 1000) mentions the fact that on at least two occasions "ark" is FEMININE
(i.e., 1 Sam. 4:17; 2 Chr. 8:11). Since this Psalm has several archaic words and forms this may answer the gender problem.

▣ "Jaar" This is a reference to Kiriath-Jearim (cf. 1 Sam. 7:1; 1 Chr. 13:1-8), where the ark was housed in a
private home for twenty years before David brought it to Jerusalem. "Jaar" is the SINGULAR form of "Jearim."

verses.zh: 我们要进他的居所，在他脚凳前下拜。
verses.en: Let us go to his dwelling place.Let us worship[NOTE:1] before his footstool.
notes: Heb “fields of the forest.” The Hebrew term יָעַר (yaʿar, “forest”) is apparently a shortened alternative name for קִרְיַת יְעָרִים (qiryat yeʿarim, “Kiriath Jearim”), the place where the ark was kept after it was released by the Philistines and from which David and his men retrieved it (see 1 Chr 13:6).
verses.commentary:
132:7 Both VERBS are COHORTATIVE PLURAL and refer to a
pilgrimage to YHWH's temple.

▣ "footstool" Both David (cf. 1 Chr. 28:2) and Solomon (1 Kgs. 8:27) recognized that the temple was not
the true dwelling place of the God of creation. David began to call the place between the wings of the Cherubim
above the mercy seat (lid of the ark; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MERCY SEAT) the place where heaven and earth, the invisible and visible, the eternal and temporal,
met (cf. Exod. 25:22)! He called it YHWH's footstool" (cf. Isa. 66:1; also note Ps. 99:5)

The imagery of Deity as having feet is part of the limits of human vocabulary.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你兴起，和你有能力的约柜同入安息之所！
verses.en: Ascend, O Lord, to your resting place,you and the ark of your strength.
verses.commentary:
132:8 "Arise" This VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used
in Num. 10:35 and 2 Chr. 6:41 to denote YHWH rising from His throne to go before His people to fight on their behalf
(cf. Ps. 3:7; 7:6; 9:19; 10:12; 44:26; 74:22; 82:8).

This verse and Ps. 132:9 seem to be an allusion to Solomon's dedication of the new temple in 2 Chr. 6:41; 1 Kings 8.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

▣ "Your resting place" YHWH is described in human terms because there is no other vocabulary
available to Bible authors (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism). The ark of the covenant and, thereby
YHWH Himself, needed/wanted a physical location for it/Him to reside/rest (cf. 1 Chr. 6:31; 28:2; 2 Chr. 6:41;
Ps. 132:8,14; Isa. 11:10; 66:1). Remember, anthropomorphic imagery does not ascribe a limit on God but on human
ability to comprehend the God of time and space (i.e., physical creation).

A new book by John Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One, uses the cosmologies of the
ANE to show that Genesis 1 is the account of YHWH building a cosmic temple (i.e., the earth) as a place to rest (cf. Gen. 2:1-3).

Hebrews 3:7 through 4:13 (cf. Ps. 95:7-11) contains a play on the word "rest" referring to three different things.

- seventh day of creation from Gen. 2:2 in Heb. 4:3,4,10

- the promised land from Numbers 13-14 in Heb. 3:11,18; 4:8

- eschatological heaven

"Rest" is both a sense of peace and a desired location of fellowship (cf. Ps. 62:1; Isa. 63:14; Jer. 31:2).

verses.zh: 愿你的祭司披上公义！愿你的圣民欢呼！
verses.en: May your priests be clothed with integrity.[NOTE:1] May your loyal followers shout for joy.
notes: Or “bow down.”
verses.commentary:
132:9 This verse has two IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES.

- be clothed ‒ BDB 527, KB 519, Qal

- sing for joy ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Piel

It is uncertain if there are two groups mentioned (i.e., priests and worshipers) or a literary parallel.

In Job 29:14 Job describes himself as clothed in righteousness. It is uncertain exactly what it
means in connection with these priests. Possibly that they reflect YHWH's character and revelations in their leadership,
lives, tasks, and duties.

This verse may reflect the festive and fearful march of the ark carried by specially dressed priests and singing Levites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "godly ones" This ADJECTIVE (BDB 339, KB 337) is a form of the
powerful covenant term hesed (BDB 336; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS). YHWH is loyal and so should His followers be!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONES

verses.zh: 求你因你仆人大卫的缘故，不要厌弃你的受膏者！
verses.en: For the sake of David, your servant,do not reject your chosen king.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “righteousness.”
verses.commentary:
132:10-12 This strophe surely alludes to 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17. Notice the conditional
element of Ps. 132:12 related to each individual descendant but also the larger purpose of God expressed in 2 Sam. 7:14-16.

Notice the sound play of so many of the VERBS of Ps. 132:10-12 starting with שׁ.

- do not turn away ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil JUSSIVE

- has sworn ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal PERFECT

- He will not turn away ‒ same root as #1 but Qal IMPERFECT

- I will set upon Your throne ‒ BDB 1011, KB 1483, Qal IMPERFECT

- if your sons will keep My covenant ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT
(notice the conditional aspect, cf. 1 Kgs. 9:4-9; Ps. 89:30-45)

132:10 "Your anointed" This is the term (BDB 603) from which the title "Messiah" comes. OT leaders
(i.e., priests, kings, and rarely, prophets) were anointed as a sign of God's call and equipping to an assigned tast.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

verses.zh: 耶和华向大卫、凭诚实起了誓，必不反覆，说：我要使你所生的坐在你的宝座上。
verses.en: The Lord made a reliable promise to David;[NOTE:1] he will not go back on his word.[NOTE:2] He said,[NOTE:3] “I will place one of your descendants[NOTE:4] on your throne.
notes: Heb “do not turn away the face of your anointed one.”
Heb “the Lord swore an oath to David [in] truth.”
Heb “he will not turn back from it.”
The words “he said” are supplied in the translation to clarify that what follows are the Lord’s words.
verses.commentary:
132:11 "The Lord has sworn to David" As David swore in Ps. 132:2, now YHWH
responds with His own oath. This oath is known as the Davidic covenant (cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17; Ps. 89:3,35).

This is a good place to discuss the conditional and unconditional nature of biblical prophecies and
covenants. The OT is a performance-based covenant. There are dire consequences to disobedience, as the Assyrian
and Neo-Babylonian exiles clearly show. All of YHWH's promises that relate to the consequences of human choice (cf.
Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19) are conditional. His promise of redemption for humankind made in His image
are unconditional.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 你的众子若守我的约和我所教训他们的法度，他们的子孙必永远坐在你的宝座上。
verses.en: If your sons keep my covenantand the rules I teach them,their sons will also sit on your throne forever.”
verses.commentary:
132:12 "covenant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "testimony" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "forever" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam).

verses.zh: 因为耶和华拣选了锡安，愿意当作自己的居所，
verses.en: Certainly[NOTE:1] the Lord has chosen Zion;he decided to make it his home.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the fruit of your body.”
Or “for.”
verses.commentary:
132:13-18 This strophe describes the things YHWH has done (Ps. 132:13-14) and will do (Ps. 132:15-18).

- He has chosen Zion (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION), Ps. 132:13-14

- He will abundantly bless (EMPHATIC INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB
of the same root, BDB 138, KB 159), Ps. 132:15a

- He will provide food, Ps. 132:15b

- the temple priests will be godly people, Ps. 132:16 (cf. 1 Chr. 6:41)

- the temple worshipers (cf. Ps. 4:3 or Levites) will sing aloud for joy (EMPHATIC INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
IMPERFECT VERB of the same root, BDB 943, KB 1247), Ps. 132:16 (cf. 1 Chr. 6:41)

- He will establish the dynasty of David in Jerusalem, Ps. 132:17

- He will defeat Israel's enemies, Ps. 132:18

verses.zh: 说：这是我永远安息之所；我要住在这里，因为是我所愿意的。
verses.en: He said,[NOTE:1] “This will be my resting place forever;I will live here, for I have chosen it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he desired it for his dwelling place.”
The words “he said” are added in the translation to clarify that what follows are the Lord’s words.

verses.zh: 我要使其中的粮食丰满，使其中的穷人饱足。
verses.en: I will abundantly supply what she needs;[NOTE:1] I will give her poor all the food they need.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for I desired it.”
Heb “I will greatly bless her provision.” The infinitive absolute is used to emphasize the verb.

verses.zh: 我要使祭司披上救恩，圣民大声欢呼！
verses.en: I will protect her priests,[NOTE:1] and her godly people will shout exuberantly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “her poor I will satisfy [with] food.”
Heb “and her priests I will clothe [with] deliverance.”
verses.commentary:
132:16 Because of the parallels of this strophe, probably "priests" (or Levites) are addressed in both lines of this verse.

▣ "godly ones" See note at verse 9.

verses.zh: 我要叫大卫的角在那里发生；我为我的受膏者预备明灯。
verses.en: There I will make David strong;[NOTE:1] I have determined that my chosen king’s dynasty will continue.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[with] shouting they will shout.” The infinitive absolute is used to emphasize the verb.

Heb “there I will cause a horn to sprout for David.” The horn of an ox underlies the metaphor (cf. Deut 33:17; 1 Kgs 22:11; Pss 18:2; 92:10). The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “exalt the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 89:17, 24; 92:10; Lam 2:17). In the ancient Near East powerful warrior-kings would sometimes compare themselves to a goring bull that used its horns to kill its enemies. For examples, see P. Miller, “El the Warrior,” HTR 60 (1967): 422-25, and R. B. Chisholm, “An Exegetical and Theological Study of Psalm 18/2 Samuel 22” (Th.D. diss., Dallas Theological Seminary, 1983), 135-36.
verses.commentary:
132:17 "the horn of David" The horn is a Hebrew idiom of power and pre-immanence (cf. Deut. 33:17;
Ps. 75:10; 92:10; 132:17; Ezek. 29:21; Luke 1:69).

▣ "to spring forth" This VERB (BDB 855, KB 1033, Hiphil IMPERFECT) may be
related to the imagery of the special Davidic King called "The Branch." See:

- SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

- full note at Isa. 11:1 online

- NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 75

The root for "crown" is נזר, which could denote

- a crown (NOUN, BDB 634)

- to consecrate (VERB, BDB 634)

- Branch (a title of the Messiah)

▣ "a lamp for Mine anointed" This is a specific usage of the light imagery that refers, not to revelation
(i.e., Ps. 18:28; 119:105; Prov. 6:23) but to a Davidic descendant on the throne of Israel (cf. v. 18b; 1 Kgs. 11:36; 15:4;
2 Kgs. 8:19; 2 Chr. 21:7). In 2 Sam. 21:17 "the lamp of Israel" refers to David himself.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

verses.zh: 我要使他的仇敌披上羞耻；但他的冠冕要在头上发光。
verses.en: I will humiliate his enemies,[NOTE:1] and his crown will shine.”
notes: Heb “I have arranged a lamp for my anointed one.” Here the “lamp” is a metaphor for the Davidic dynasty (see 1 Kgs 11:36).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is obviously a Psalm about

- God's promises to David in 2 Sam. 7:12-16; 2 Chr. 6:16 (see brief discussion of "The Davidic Covenant" in
NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 507-508)

- God's choice of Mt. Moriah as the place for His presence to dwell (cf. Deut. 12:5,11,14,18, 21,26; 14:23-25; 15:20;
16:2,6,11,15; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2; 31:11, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH)

- The results of God's presence and Israel's covenant obedience are

- to abundantly bless her provision, Ps. 132:15

- to satisfy her hunger, Ps. 132:15

- wonderful worship, Ps. 132:16

- God's king exalted, Ps. 132:17

- the destruction of the Davidic king's enemies, Ps. 132:17

- For a good brief discussion of the theology of Zion see NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 959 and 512.
